correctness.rationale: A fresh exact replay reconstructed the two labeled graphs and obtained λ⁶(λ²−4)⁴(λ²−16) for both adjacency matrices. The explicit D describes the noncube mate: vertices 0 and 1 share three neighbors, whereas distinct vertices of Q₄ share either zero or two. Van Dam §3 reports that there are exactly two graphs with this spectrum, identifying this matrix independently of the unretrieved MathWorld matrix. Exhausting all 2¹⁶ vertex subsets per graph gives face counts (1,16,88,208,228,132,56,16,2) and (1,16,88,208,228,128,56,16,2), with no larger faces, proving the exact polynomial difference. The independent replay reconstructed the pivot matchings, checked the supplied topological positions at all 2836 and 2816 directed Hasse incidences respectively, and separately performed a topological sort. The nonempty-face matchings leave exactly one 0-cell and 3 or 7 three-cells, with no other cells. Discrete Morse theory therefore gives the stated CW homotopy types, and all three-cells attach to the single point. This certifies the integral wedge statements, not just ranks over a field. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed; fresh replay and output are at /workspace/branches/dd57e65a-67b9-4ed3-a6df-fde3dcc320b9/replay_hoffman_q4.py and replay.log in the same directory.
